input.quote: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
input.rationale: Section 4.2 imposes a stipulated sum payable by the Company (our client) whenever the Company terminates — a liquidated early-termination payment equal to (trailing 12-month Net Sales − $800,000) ÷ 2, payable in eight quarterly instalments. This fails the fallback: the amount is measured against gross Net Sales rather than fees and is uncapped, so it far exceeds three months' fees (fees are only 30% of Net Sales above $11,000 per month; e.g. at $2M annual Net Sales the payment would be roughly $600,000 versus roughly $140,000 of three months' fees). It is also triggered by any Company termination, including the ordinary 90-day non-renewal right in Section 4.1 and (apart from the narrow Section 1.6 launch-failure carve-out) termination for HDI's own default. We therefore proposed deleting Section 4.2 to reach the preferred position of no Customer-payable liquidated damages, noting the three-month fee cap as an acceptable fallback if a fee is unavoidable.

proposal.summary: Delete the Company-payable Termination Payment in Section 4.2 (and conform the Section 4 heading).
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the Termination Payment, which requires us to pay a stipulated sum (half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales over $800,000) simply for exercising our termination right; our playbook does not accept liquidated damages or termination penalties payable by the Company. If an early-termination fee is unavoidable, we can accept one capped at three months' fees as the sole such amount.
